maya: Heads-up — I hit KV cache OOM spikes during the 11:15 perf run after the kernel-routing tweak. Repro notes and short logs below. @trent can you take a look?

perfbot: deploy-bot rolled out kernel preference "mha_kernel_v3" to p-prod at 2026-03-15T11:00Z (canary 20% -> 100%).

trent: Which model/seq-dist? Any quick numbers?

maya: Quick paste from the run: ```
model: llama2-13b
kernel_routing: preferred mha_kernel_v3, fallback aten_fused
batch_window_ms: 8 -> 8 (no change)
token_budget_target: 5120
seq_len_p90: 640
throughput_tokens/s: 420k -> 410k (minor)
p99 latency: 380ms -> 620ms (regression)
kv_cache_mem_peak: 12.8GB -> 18.3GB (per-GPU)
OOMs: 3/12 GPUs in canary group
```

li: Thanks — preliminary theory: mha_kernel_v3 keeps intermediate KV tensors in a denser layout (faster attention kernel) but it prevents a cheaper quantized KV compression path we were using with aten_fused. That increases per-token KV footprint. With batching heuristics unchanged, token-admission allowed larger aggregated KV, so memory headroom got eaten.

anya: We should treat KV headroom as a first-class admission constraint. Proposal sketch: keep soft_headroom = 20% of free GPU memory. Compute expected_kv = avg_kv_per_token * tokens_in_incoming_batch. Reject/admit based on expected_kv + current_kv <= free_mem - soft_headroom. If fail, try splitting batch or mark as deferred.

devon: Also noticed queueing/backpressure: when `batch_window_ms` is small we still pack many requests because arrival bursts coincide. The change to kernel_route increased per-request KV so the same burst now overflows. We should have an adaptive token_budget_target that reduces during high KV pressure.

trent: Quick admission pseudo: ```
free = gpu_free_bytes()
headroom = free * 0.20
expected = avg_kv_per_token * tokens_in_batch
if expected + current_kv > free - headroom:
    if tokens_in_batch > min_split: split_batch()
    else: set_priority("defer")
else: admit()
```
This keeps logic simple and lets us avoid OOMs without immediate hard rejects.

li: I ran a microprofiling pass on a single GPU with the two kernels (short synthetic mix). Numbers: 
- mha_kernel_v3: avg_kv_per_token = 245 bytes/token, peak_kv_per_batch = 13.1GB for 53k tokens aggregate
- aten_fused: avg_kv_per_token = 160 bytes/token, peak_kv_per_batch = 8.6GB for same tokens
That delta explains the ~5-6GB extra and OOMs.

maya: Good data. So short-term mitigations: (1) lower kernel preference weight for mha_kernel_v3 for high seq-len routes; (2) implement soft_headroom admission check; (3) expose a metric kv_expected_vs_free on per-GPU dashboards.

perfbot: scheduled perf run with admission-rule patch at 2026-03-15T11:45Z (canary group only).

anya: Also propose a fallback compaction pass: if admission would fail, attempt a quick lossy compaction step on cold KV entries (cheap quantize) before rejecting. Might buy us headroom for a few big bursts. Needs microbench.

devon: One more: our batch shaper currently prioritizes latency SLOs. When KV pressure is high we should switch to conservative shaping (smaller token cap) even if latency p50 degrades slightly. Add a toggle in queue policy: kv_pressure_mode -> reduce_token_budget_by(30%).

trent: I'll open a small PR that: adjusts kernel selector weight, adds soft_headroom admission, and a new metric. We can keep the compaction pass in a follow-up.

maya: Thanks. @li can you run the perf harness with the synthetic mix and a real arrival trace (11:15) after the PR and paste numbers? Aim to confirm p99 < 450ms and no OOMs.

li: On it — will run in 20m and post results here.

sre-bot: incident note created: INC-2026-0315-KV-001 — "KV memory pressure during kernel routing rollout". Pager disabled (canary scope).

maya: TL;DR plan in one line: make KV-aware admission + temporary kernel weighting, add dashboard + schedule verification run. :thumbsup:
